page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this server features 40 dedicated physical cores with 40 vCPUs, providing a direct one-to-one mapping without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.4 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge demonstrates solid compute and memory throughput. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions and AVX512_VNNI for vector neural network instructions. Memory performance shows a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and a write bandwidth of 36.66 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the instance delivers a Geekbench multi-core score of 11735.0, with notable performance in software compilation (28295.0) and ray tracing (30187.0). Database operations on Passmark score at 13891.08, while Redis SET operations reach 34.66 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is its lack of local storage and relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.4 GB per core, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive datasets. However, the dedicated core allocation and high 3.1 GHz clock speed offer reliable, non-shared compute performance, making it a cost-efficient choice for compute-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. This instance is suitable for high-throughput web serving (achieving 23.2 GB/sec in static web serving tests), multi-threaded decompression tasks, software compilation, and moderate-sized machine learning inference, such as running a 7B parameter LLM at 12.33 tokens per second for text generation.
